name: Cerebral palsy
one_line: Cerebral palsy shapes how a child moves, not who they are. With the right therapy and support, your child has real room to grow.
who_this_is_for: Parents whose baby or young child has cerebral palsy, or whose doctor is watching their movement and muscle tone.
red_flags: A seizure lasting more than 5 minutes: call 108
Choking, or coughing and struggling to breathe during feeds
Losing skills your child already had

track.label: Therapy notes, reports and appointments, in one place

faq.a: Cerebral palsy is a group of conditions that affect movement and posture. It comes from a difference or injury in the developing brain, before, during or soon after birth. The brain injury does not get worse over time, though a child's needs change as they grow.

Doctors often notice stiff or floppy muscles, or movements that look different, in the first year or two. Your paediatrician or a paediatric neurologist may suggest a brain scan and a detailed movement check. Your doctor decides which tests are needed.

Physiotherapy, occupational therapy and speech therapy are the main supports, and they work best as part of daily life at home. Your therapist will show you how to hold, play with and position your child. Some children also need medicines, splints or surgery, and your doctor decides.

faq.q: Where can we get help in India?
faq.a: District Early Intervention Centres (DEICs) under the RBSK programme offer therapy for young children. Cerebral palsy is also recognised under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, which can open access to support. Your paediatrician can guide you on certificates and schemes.
